$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=-\pi /2} & =-17\operatorname{csc}⁡(17x)\operatorname{cot}⁡(17x){|}_{x=-\pi /2} \\  & =-17\operatorname{csc}⁡(17\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2}))\operatorname{cot}⁡(17\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =-17\operatorname{csc}⁡(-\frac{17\pi }{2})\operatorname{cot}⁡(-\frac{17\pi }{2}) \\  & =-17\cdot (-1)\cdot 0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

First, the slope of $y = f(x)$ at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ is given by $f'\left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right).$

We will calculate $f'(x)$ using the chain rule. We express $f(x)$ as the composite function
$$
f = 3\sec{u}, \qquad u = \pi x^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives
$$
\dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d u} = 3\sec{u}\tan{u}, \qquad\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 2\pi x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d x} & = \dfrac{\textrm d f}{\textrm d u} \cdot \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x}\\[5pt]

&= 3\sec{u}\tan{u} \cdot 2\pi x \\[5pt]

&= 2\pi x 3\sec{\left(\pi x^{2}\right)}\tan{\left(\pi x^{2}\right)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$, we find 

$$
\begin{aligned}
f'\left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right) &= 2\pi \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 3\sec{\left[\pi\cdot\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2}\right]}\tan{\left[\pi\cdot\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2}\right]} \\[5pt]
&= \pi 3\sec{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)} \tan{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)} \\[5pt]
&= 3\pi \cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot 1 \\[5pt]
&= 3\pi\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y = f(x)$ at $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$ is $\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{3\pi\sqrt{2}}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}

f'(1) & =\dfrac 1 5\csc^2\left(1-\dfrac 1 5 \right) \\[3pt]
	& =\dfrac 1 5\csc^2\left(\dfrac 4 5 \right) .
       
    \end{aligned}
$$
Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve $y = f(x)$ at $x = 1$ is $\dfrac{1}{5}\csc^2\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right).$
